Never fall back to main-Agent production editing. `fstar-debug` is core-automatic: route to it when a native dispatch fails twice (at most one automatic retry, with the prior reason) or a repair shows no progress.\n\n## Extension negotiation\n\nPackage IDs are exactly `planning-review`, `persistent-task`, `multi-agent`, `project-governance`, and `tool-capability`. Grants are independent. Reuse an existing grant. Otherwise explain benefit and cost and recommend only one highest-value package. Default to full scope, allow explicit custom included/excluded capabilities, but never remove implement/check separation, repair after failure, or user-only completion. After refusal, continue the minimal loop and do not ask again unless new facts materially change value or cost. Planning authorization does not create task.json. Mid-work authorization imports valid work without redoing it.\n\n- Planning/review need: negotiate planning-review, then `fstar-clarify`/`fstar-doc`; reviewed documents automatically route to `fstar-plan`, then execute without another plan approval.\n- Persistence/recovery need: negotiate persistent-task, then task commands and `fstar-continue`.\n- Enhanced parallel/research/change propagation need: negotiate multi-agent; base implement/check remains available without it.\n- Initialized-project governance or durable knowledge need: negotiate project-governance, then `fstar-init`/`fstar-learn`.\n- Capability binding or classification need: negotiate tool-capability, then `fstar-tools`.\n\nA recall intent queries indexed knowledge and archived task listing with sources and applicability differences; it does not restore an archived task and has no recall skill. Continue resumes only the current task and never scans archive candidates. Only after a successful `fstar-archive` operation may routing show other long-unarchived candidates; reminders never auto-archive. `fstar-help` explains observed installed entries only.\n\n### role \u2014 agents/fstar-implement.md\n\n---\nname: fstar-implement\ndescription: \"Implement assigned scope and return verifiable delivery facts. \u5b9e\u65bd\u6307\u5b9a\u8303\u56f4\u5e76\u8fd4\u56de\u53ef\u9a8c\u8bc1\u4e8b\u5b9e\u3002\"\n---\n\n# fstar-implement\n\n## Allowed paths and rules\n\nWrite only allowed product/test paths. Small-step self-check is not the independent check. Stop writing handed-off scope.\n\n## Dispatch input\n\nFirst line is `Active task: <path>` or `Active task: session-only`. Require dispatch_id, task_ref, role, plan_item_ids, baseline, input versions/fingerprints, allowed_paths, read_context, required validation, and completion/block/failure conditions. Read complete applicable context; summaries do not replace source bodies.\n\n## Return\n\nReturn dispatch_id, role, status, changed_paths, artifact references, actual validation facts, measured duration/retries, blockers, input baseline, and delivery baseline. A role card is a protocol, not a security sandbox, and must not claim that a host worker has started.\n\nActive task: session-only\nRole: implement. ## Run consolidation — 2026-10-30

Python 3.9.6, Darwin. Fixture tests use temporary project, user, runtime and host roots. The command records above include argv, environment, stdin, exit status, stdout and stderr; direct file setup and internal API steps are identified separately. Earlier failures remain above. Two early exploratory runs predated ledger instrumentation: 6 tests, 2 failures and 4 errors; then 6 tests, 3 failures and 2 errors. Their complete output was not preserved, so only those totals are reported. A later harness-runner name collision prevented unittest startup; it was repaired before the evidence-producing runs. Fixture corrections are not product fixes.

| Scenario | Verdict | Evidence level and limits |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | FAIL | fixture-test: lifecycle proceeds through orphan and archive views; status omits promised check provenance; check outcome rows are explicitly synthetic fixture review outcomes, not actual test runs. Completed-task rollback after doc edit, unrelated-evidence isolation, and post-archive state/status are not proven. |
| S2 | FAIL | fixture-test: no-project session-only CLI rejected; explicit uninitialized project root permits register/harvest without metadata writes. Hook routing is injected. Native session routing/dispatch not proven. Cross-scenario summary is a reference, not an independent assertion. |
| S3 | PARTIAL | fixture-test: extension/provenance write and extension-shaped provenance rejection observed. Reverse capability-shaped extension write not established; direct mutation limitation observed. |
| S4 | PARTIAL | fixture-test: registry, weak probe, binding, unbind, availability and provenance tested; separate unclassified manual candidate not asserted. |
| S5 | PARTIAL | fixture-test: four tiers and conflict, proposal-bound approval, and hook injection tested. Mutation of an index and reference as a group is not established by this fixture. |
| S6 | PARTIAL | fixture-test installation/doctor/uninstall; hook plan reports observed-schema or unverified-schema; real host delivery blocked. Snapshot covers real ~/.fstar and ~/.claude/settings.json, not the complete ~/.claude tree. |

### Contract findings for coordinator

1. S2-3a: with no --project and uninitialized cwd, session-only dispatch exits 2 with project_not_initialized. Runtime-dispatch child T9 and this child S2-3 promise uninitialized-directory session-only CLI; parent describes explicit task CLI as requiring data, so coordinator should resolve that boundary. `_handle_dispatch` / `_handle_harvest` call `_service_from_args` before session-only short-circuit (src/fstar/dispatch.py:770, 836; src/fstar/cli.py:147). Explicit --project to an uninitialized temporary root succeeds and writes no metadata. No source changes were made.
2. S1-8: acceptance status returns five result labels but omits run_id, environment, and delivery from check entries despite child design §2 promising these (src/fstar/evidence.py:363). Check evidence itself receives those fields. Coordinator should decide whether to change status output or correct the design contract.

### Coverage and outstanding work

| Preceding area / acceptance group | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Task state, confirmations, evidence, archive and templates | S1, with gaps above |
| Runtime routing and dispatch | S1/S2; real host delivery blocked |
| Extensions, capabilities and tools | S2/S3/S4; incomplete reverse-shape/manual-candidate checks |
| Knowledge | S5; grouped index/reference mutation not verified |
| Installer, hook registration and doctor | S6 fixture-test and observed-schema only |

Unverified matrix cells include: single-leaf no-check acceptance beyond the explicit leaf gate, archive post-read behavior, completed-task doc invalidation rollback, stale-check unrelated evidence isolation, exact user deferral semantics, full zero-write proof for every S2 step, actual manual scan candidates, confirmed group update of index/references, and reverse cross-shape authorization rejection. Per-step callbacks and subprocess output are preserved, but not every auxiliary filesystem assertion is paired with its own verdict record. Fixture check evidence uses synthetic review outcomes and is not a real independent checker result.

Withdrawn or not delivered by design: seven-state lifecycle vocabulary, independent review-log, test-cases approval package, `fstar spec check`, and `skillOverrides`. Direct file editing can insert extension-like dictionaries into capabilities because validation checks only dictionary shape. CLI/API separation is observed rather than a live-agent guarantee.

Blocked: live-delivery=0. Actual Claude/Codex event delivery requires user authorization to register hooks in real host settings and a real host session; native dispatch/steering/interruption and skill trigger/listing require user participation in that session. npm package-name conflict and template commit 674bea3 content/license require network access; Codex user-level installation path requires observation in a real Codex host. No real host settings were written.

It decides what to invoke before invocation; commands remain responsible for state validation.\n\n## Always-available minimal loop\n\nClarify the goal in conversation, invoke `fstar-execute` through the host native implement role, invoke independent `fstar-check`, return every failed check to repair and recheck, then wait for explicit user confirmation. Never fall back to main-Agent production editing. `fstar-debug` is core-automatic: route to it when a native dispatch fails twice (at most one automatic retry, with the prior reason) or a repair shows no progress.\n\n## Extension negotiation\n\nPackage IDs are exactly `planning-review`, `persistent-task`, `multi-agent`, `project-governance`, and `tool-capability`. Default to full scope, allow explicit custom included/excluded capabilities, but never remove implement/check separation, repair after failure, or user-only completion. After refusal, continue the minimal loop and do not ask again unless new facts materially change value or cost. Planning authorization does not create task.json. Mid-work authorization imports valid work without redoing it.\n\n- Planning/review need: negotiate planning-review, then `fstar-clarify`/`fstar-doc`; reviewed documents automatically route to `fstar-plan`, then execute without another plan approval.\n- Persistence/recovery need: negotiate persistent-task, then task commands and `fstar-continue`.\n- Enhanced parallel/research/change propagation need: negotiate multi-agent; base implement/check remains available without it.\n- Initialized-project governance or durable knowledge need: negotiate project-governance, then `fstar-init`/`fstar-learn`.\n- Capability binding or classification need: negotiate tool-capability, then `fstar-tools`.\n\nA recall intent queries indexed knowledge and archived task listing with sources and applicability differences; it does not restore an archived task and has no recall skill. Continue resumes only the current task and never scans archive candidates. Only after a successful `fstar-archive` operation may routing show other long-unarchived candidates; reminders never auto-archive. `fstar-help` explains observed installed entries only.\n\nNo initialized fstar project found; task bookkeeping skipped (this is normal outside an initialized project).\n\nLearn candidates attach only to existing session/result/recovery/archive nodes; no per-turn scan and no standalone candidate ledger exists.\n",

Only after a successful `fstar-archive` operation may routing show other long-unarchived candidates; reminders never auto-archive. `fstar-help` explains observed installed entries only.\n\n### role — agents/fstar-implement.md\n\n---\nname: fstar-implement\ndescription: \"Implement assigned scope and return verifiable delivery facts. 实施指定范围并返回可验证事实。\"\n---\n\n# fstar-implement\n\n## Allowed paths and rules\n\nWrite only allowed product/test paths. Small-step self-check is not the independent check. Stop writing handed-off scope.\n\n## Dispatch input\n\nFirst line is `Active task: <path>` or `Active task: session-only`. Require dispatch_id, task_ref, role, plan_item_ids, baseline, input versions/fingerprints, allowed_paths, read_context, required validation, and completion/block/failure conditions. Read complete applicable context; summaries do not replace source bodies.\n\n## Return\n\nReturn dispatch_id, role, status, changed_paths, artifact references, actual validation facts, measured duration/retries, blockers, input baseline, and delivery baseline. A role card is a protocol, not a security sandbox, and must not claim that a host worker has started.\n\nActive task: session-only\nRole: implement. Read complete applicable context; summaries do not replace source bodies.\nIf any input is listed under 'Unloaded inputs', you MUST read it in full before executing.\nassertion: role card + session-only line",

Mid-work authorization imports valid work without redoing it.\n\nBefore consuming a package member, check that member is in the current grant's `included` list; `excluded` and unlisted members are unavailable. Task recovery reads the task's `extensions` records; never substitute `capabilities`, which records tool facts. For session-only work, retain the authorization records returned by `extension enable` in the caller's session and pass them as the `extensions` array in hook and dispatch JSON payloads. On disable remove that record from subsequent payloads. Separate CLI invocations cannot remember these grants. Use the editor and document check only when their respective members are included.\n- Persistence/recovery need: use task, evidence, lease, events, recovery and archive only when their corresponding members are included; `fstar-continue` requires `recovery`.\n- Enhanced collaboration: require `research`, `parallel-implement`, `version-injection`, or `change-propagation` for the respective enhancement; base implement/check remains available.\n- Governance: use specs, knowledge, rules, or memory only with the corresponding included member; route learning according to its actual destination.\n- Tool capabilities: use contracts, bindings, classification, validation, or fallback only with the corresponding included package member. These five members are distinct from the five tool capability contracts.\n\nA recall intent queries indexed knowledge and archived task listing with sources and applicability differences; it does not restore an archived task and has no recall skill. Continue resumes only the current task and never scans archive candidates. Only after a successful `fstar-archive` operation may routing show other long-unarchived candidates; reminders never auto-archive. `fstar-help` explains observed installed entries only.\n\nExtension members in this context: {}\n\nNo initialized fstar project found; task bookkeeping skipped (this is normal outside an initialized project).\n\nLearn candidates attach only to existing session/result/recovery/archive nodes; no per-turn scan and no standalone candidate ledger exists.\n",

After refusal, continue the minimal loop and do not ask again unless new facts materially change value or cost. Planning authorization does not create task.json. Mid-work authorization imports valid work without redoing it.\n\nBefore consuming a package member, check that member is in the current grant's `included` list; `excluded` and unlisted members are unavailable. Task recovery reads the task's `extensions` records; never substitute `capabilities`, which records tool facts. For session-only work, retain the authorization records returned by `extension enable` in the caller's session and pass them as the `extensions` array in hook and dispatch JSON payloads. On disable remove that record from subsequent payloads. Separate CLI invocations cannot remember these grants. These records guide cooperating callers and are not a same-permission security boundary.\n\n- Planning/review need: use `fstar-clarify` only with `clarify`, `fstar-doc` only for included `prd` or `design`, and `fstar-plan` only with `plan`. Use the editor and document check only when their respective members are included.\n- Persistence/recovery need: use task, evidence, lease, events, recovery and archive only when their corresponding members are included; `fstar-continue` requires `recovery`.\n- Enhanced collaboration: require `research`, `parallel-implement`, `version-injection`, or `change-propagation` for the respective enhancement; base implement/check remains available.\n- Governance: use specs, knowledge, rules, or memory only with the corresponding included member; route learning according to its actual destination. Project initialization precedes project governance and includes an initial proposal-only tool scan; binding requires user confirmation. The current CLI initializes the skeleton but does not yet run that scan or apply collected context; report those gaps.\n- Tool capabilities: use contracts, bindings, classification, validation, or fallback only with the corresponding included package member. These five members are distinct from the five tool capability contracts.\n\nA recall intent queries indexed knowledge and archived task listing with sources and applicability differences; it does not restore an archived task and has no recall skill. Continue resumes only the current task and never scans archive candidates. Only after a successful `fstar-archive` operation may routing show other long-unarchived candidates; reminders never auto-archive. `fstar-help` explains observed installed entries only.\n\nExtension members in this context: {}\n\nNo initialized fstar project found; task bookkeeping skipped (this is normal outside an initialized project).\n\nLearn candidates attach only to existing session/result/recovery/archive nodes; no per-turn scan and no standalone candidate ledger exists.\n",

Mid-work authorization imports valid work without redoing it.\n\nBefore consuming a package member, check that member is in the current grant's `included` list; `excluded` and unlisted members are unavailable. Task recovery reads the task's `extensions` records; never substitute `capabilities`, which records tool facts. For session-only work, retain the authorization records returned by `extension enable` in the caller's session and pass them as the `extensions` array in hook and dispatch JSON payloads. On disable remove that record from subsequent payloads. Separate CLI invocations cannot remember these grants. Project initialization precedes project governance and includes an initial proposal-only tool scan; binding requires user confirmation. The current CLI initializes the skeleton but does not yet run that scan or apply collected context; report those gaps.\n- Tool capabilities: use contracts, bindings, classification, validation, or fallback only with the corresponding included package member. These five members are distinct from the five tool capability contracts.\n\nA recall intent queries indexed knowledge and archived task listing with sources and applicability differences; it does not restore an archived task and has no recall skill. Continue resumes only the current task and never scans archive candidates. It decides what to invoke before invocation; commands remain responsible for state validation.\n\n## Always-available minimal loop\n\nClarify the goal in conversation, invoke `fstar-execute` through the host native implement role, invoke independent `fstar-check`, return every failed check to repair and recheck, then wait for explicit user confirmation. Session nodes are not persisted and no fstar metadata is created. This does not prohibit delivery files. Never fall back to main-Agent production editing. `fstar-debug` is core-automatic: route to it when a native dispatch fails twice (at most one automatic retry, with the prior reason) or a repair shows no progress.\n\n## Extension negotiation\n\nPackage IDs are exactly `planning-review`, `persistent-task`, `multi-agent`, `project-governance`, and `tool-capability`. Grants are independent. Reuse an existing grant. Otherwise explain benefit and cost and recommend only one highest-value package. Default to full scope, allow explicit custom included/excluded capabilities, but never remove implement/check separation, repair after failure, or user-only completion. After refusal, continue the minimal loop and do not ask again unless new facts materially change value or cost. Planning authorization does not create task.json. Mid-work authorization imports valid work without redoing it.\n\nBefore consuming a package member, check that member is in the current grant's `included` list; `excluded` and unlisted members are unavailable. Task recovery reads the task's `extensions` records; never substitute `capabilities`, which records tool facts. For session-only work, retain the authorization records returned by `extension enable` in the caller's session and pass them as the `extensions` array in hook and dispatch JSON payloads. These records guide cooperating callers and are not a same-permission security boundary.\n\n- Planning/review need: use `fstar-clarify` only with `clarify`, `fstar-doc` only for included `prd` or `design`, and `fstar-plan` only with `plan`. Use the editor and document check only when their respective members are included.\n- Persistence/recovery need: use task, evidence, lease, events, recovery and archive only when their corresponding members are included; `fstar-continue` requires `recovery`.\n- Enhanced collaboration: require `research`, `parallel-implement`, `version-injection`, or `change-propagation` for the respective enhancement; base implement/check remains available.\n- Governance: use specs, knowledge, rules, or memory only with the corresponding included member; route learning according to its actual destination. Project initialization precedes project governance and includes an initial proposal-only tool scan; binding requires user confirmation. The current CLI initializes the skeleton but does not yet run that scan or apply collected context; report those gaps.\n- Tool capabilities: use contracts, bindings, classification, validation, or fallback only with the corresponding included package member. It decides what to invoke before invocation; commands remain responsible for state validation.\n\n## Always-available minimal loop\n\nClarify the goal in conversation, invoke `fstar-execute` through the host native implement role, invoke independent `fstar-check`, return every failed check to repair and recheck, then wait for explicit user confirmation. Session nodes are not persisted and no fstar metadata is created. This does not prohibit delivery files. Never fall back to main-Agent production editing. `fstar-debug` is core-automatic: route to it when a native dispatch fails twice (at most one automatic retry, with the prior reason) or a repair shows no progress.\n\n## Extension negotiation\n\nPackage IDs are exactly `planning-review`, `persistent-task`, `multi-agent`, `project-governance`, and `tool-capability`. Grants are independent. Reuse an existing grant. Otherwise explain benefit and cost and recommend only one highest-value package. Default to full scope, allow explicit custom included/excluded capabilities, but never remove implement/check separation, repair after failure, or user-only completion. After refusal, continue the minimal loop and do not ask again unless new facts materially change value or cost. Planning authorization does not create task.json. Mid-work authorization imports valid work without redoing it.\n\nBefore consuming a package member, check that member is in the current grant's `included` list; `excluded` and unlisted members are unavailable. Task recovery reads the task's `extensions` records; never substitute `capabilities`, which records tool facts. For session-only work, retain the authorization records returned by `extension enable` in the caller's session and pass them as the `extensions` array in hook and dispatch JSON payloads. On disable remove that record from subsequent payloads. Separate CLI invocations cannot remember these grants. These records guide cooperating callers and are not a same-permission security boundary.\n\n- Planning/review need: use `fstar-clarify` only with `clarify`, `fstar-doc` only for included `prd` or `design`, and `fstar-plan` only with `plan`.
